reference_root_cause: The orders-api v3.2.0 release introduced a connection leak in ReportScheduler.exportDaily, which opened database connections without releasing them and exhausted the 20-connection pool.
reference_summary: Minutes after the v3.2.0 deploy of orders-api, the ReportScheduler.exportDaily job leaked database connections until the pool was exhausted. Requests then timed out waiting for connections and /orders p99 latency breached the SLO, while the database itself stayed healthy. Rolling back to v3.1.9 released the leaked connections and restored normal latency. The failing nightly-report cron and the cache hit-ratio dip were unrelated.

Day4 11:03:44 ERROR ingest-svc: producer send failed: NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS, retrying
Day4 11:05:10 WARN analytics-api: freshness SLA breached: newest event 9m old
Day4 11:21:38 INFO oncall: broker-3 disk 100% — largest dirs are clickstream-* segments spanning 22 days
Day4 11:29:03 INFO ops: retention.ms for 'clickstream' reverted to 604800000 (7d), old segments deleting

reference_root_cause: A retention configuration change on the clickstream topic (7 days to 30 days) quadrupled stored segment data until broker-3's disk filled, taking its log dir and partitions offline.
reference_summary: Three days after the clickstream topic's retention was raised from 7 to 30 days, accumulated log segments filled broker-3's disk. The broker shut down its log directory on the ENOSPC error, partitions went offline, producers failed with NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS, and analytics freshness breached its SLA. Reverting the retention to 7 days and deleting old segments restored the broker and cleared the errors. The consumer-lag and kernel warnings were unrelated noise.

reference_summary: A feature flag intended for staging enabled verbose request tracing on all production search-api traffic. Log volume jumped 42x and trace serialization consumed ~60% of CPU, driving p99 latency far past the SLO; autoscaling to max replicas didn't help because every pod paid the logging overhead, and the log pipeline started dropping events. Disabling the flag returned CPU, latency, and log volume to baseline within two minutes. The brief packet loss on rack R12 was unrelated.

10:05:33 INFO waf: rule 921110 moved from block to monitor mode by security team
11:47:19 WARN node worker-5: chronyd exited (segfault), clock discipline stopped
13:22:08 WARN auth-svc (pod auth-5 on worker-5): token issued with iat 13:25:41 — issuer clock ahead?
13:24:51 ERROR api-gateway: 401 token validation failed: token used before issued (nbf in future)
13:25:02 ERROR api-gateway: 401 token validation failed: token used before issued (nbf in future)
13:26:33 WARN support: login failures reported by ~5% of users, retry sometimes works
13:29:10 ERROR api-gateway: 401 token validation failed: token used before issued (nbf in future)
13:31:47 INFO oncall: failures correlate with tokens minted by pod auth-5 only; other pods clean
13:33:20 INFO oncall: rollback of auth-svc v2.4.4 considered — but pods on other nodes run same version without errors, deploy ruled out
13:36:55 INFO ops: worker-5 system clock is 3m42s ahead of NTP reference; chronyd not running since 11:47
13:39:02 INFO ops: chronyd restarted on worker-5, clock stepped back to reference
13:40:11 INFO auth-svc: tokens from auth-5 validating cleanly
13:42:00 INFO api-gateway: 401 rate back to baseline 0.05%
13:55:12 INFO ops: added alert on node clock offset > 500ms
reference_root_cause: chronyd crashed on worker-5 and the node's clock drifted almost 4 minutes ahead, so tokens minted by the auth pod on that node had future timestamps and failed nbf/iat validation at the gateway.
reference_summary: After the NTP daemon segfaulted on worker-5, the node's clock drifted about 3m42s ahead. The auth-svc pod on that node began issuing tokens with future iat/nbf claims, which the api-gateway rejected as 'used before issued', causing intermittent 401s for roughly 5% of users — only requests whose tokens came from the skewed pod. Restarting chronyd and stepping the clock fixed validation immediately; the v2.4.4 deploy and the WAF rule change were unrelated.

02:12:30 ERROR tax-svc: inbound QPS 9x baseline from payments-api, 429s
02:13:02 WARN api-gateway: /charge error rate 17%
02:14:11 INFO oncall: LD stream still down; pods on worker-3 are the only ones on the default
02:16:40 INFO flags: LaunchDarkly stream restored, 'charge_sync_legacy_path' evaluated false
02:17:05 INFO payments-api: pods refreshed flag, legacy path off
02:18:20 INFO payments-api: p99 360ms, tax-svc QPS back to baseline
reference_root_cause: After a kubelet restart, payments-api could not reach LaunchDarkly and used the baked-in default charge_sync_legacy_path=true, which enabled a retired sync tax path; the running image had not changed.
reference_summary: A kernel live-patch restarted pods on worker-3. Those processes missed the LaunchDarkly stream and fell back to a binary default that turned 'charge_sync_legacy_path' on, even though the live flag was false. The legacy path stampeded tax-svc, /charge p99 and error rate broke, and there was no new payments-api code. Restoring the flag stream flipped the default off and latency recovered. The GC pause was incidental.

reference_root_cause: spark-etl-4401 ran without CPU limits on worker-7 and starved session-api pods of CPU, so kubelet liveness probes failed; session-api itself was not the fault.
reference_summary: A limitless Spark ETL job landed on worker-7 and consumed nearly all 16 cores. session-api pods on that node started failing liveness probes and restarting, which showed up as /session errors. HPA added replicas on other nodes and did not help the victim pods. The v2.8.1 deploy was already healthy. When the batch job finished, CPU and probes recovered. The paged service was the noisy-neighbor victim, not the cause.

source: curated: one AZ dependency is down; retries fan the symptom into every service (red herrings: multi-service 5xx)

18:10:20 WARN payments-api (az-a): healthy, p99 90ms, redis-sessions-az-a 0.2ms
18:10:28 ERROR redis-sessions-az-b: node host maintenance, ENETUNREACH from all az-b clients
18:10:40 INFO hpa: checkout-api, cart-api, storefront all scaling — 5xx still concentrated on az-b callers
18:11:02 INFO oncall: az-a and az-c error rates 0.4%; az-b 70% of 5xx
18:12:15 INFO ops: blocked az-b redis-sessions in the service mesh, traffic pinned to az-a/az-c
18:13:00 INFO storefront: 5xx back to 0.3%
18:14:40 INFO aws: az-b redis maintenance window posted 40m earlier in the infra channel, missed by app oncall
reference_root_cause: redis-sessions in az-b became unreachable (ENETUNREACH) during host maintenance; sticky retries kept sending checkout/cart/storefront traffic at the dead AZ instead of failing over.
reference_summary: Host maintenance took redis-sessions-az-b off the network. payments-api in az-b started timing out, and checkout, cart, and storefront retried without jitter or AZ failover, so 5xx appeared in many user-facing services. payments-api in az-a stayed healthy. Pinning traffic off az-b cleared the errors. Autoscaling the frontends did not help because the dependency in one AZ was dead. The multi-service symptom was a retry fan-out, not a platform-wide code bug.

12:05:12 INFO notify-api: running image v3.5.4, config checksum unchanged across the rollback
12:08:44 INFO secrets: vault lease smtp-notify-prod last renewed 90 days ago, vendor rotated the SMTP password at 12:00 UTC
12:12:02 INFO secrets: smtp-notify-prod password updated in vault and synced to notify-api
12:12:30 INFO notify-api: SMTP AUTH succeeded, drain of 4k queued mails started
12:18:00 INFO api-gateway: user reports of missing reset mail stopped
reference_root_cause: The SMTP vendor rotated the notify-api password at 12:00 UTC; the v3.6.0 template deploy was unrelated, which a successful rollback proved because AUTH 535 continued on v3.5.4.
reference_summary: Password-reset mail stopped at 12:00 with SMTP 535 authentication failures. On-call rolled back notify-api v3.6.0 to v3.5.4; the rollback completed cleanly and the 535s continued on the old image with the same config checksum. Vault still had a 90-day-old SMTP secret; the vendor had rotated the password at 12:00. Updating the secret restored AUTH and drained the queue. The same-day deploy was a decoy.
